Check the decomposition of a relative-importance network

Source: R/relimp.R
lmg_certificate.Rd

lmg_certificate() checks the decomposition stored in a relative-importance network from relimp_network(). Such a network divides the \(R^2\) of each variable, regressed on all the others, among its predictors; it is defined by a decomposition rather than as the optimum of an objective, and two identities must hold for that decomposition to be correct.

The shares a node receives must sum exactly to its \(R^2\), which is the efficiency property of the Shapley value. And that \(R^2\) must be the one implied by the correlation matrix, which has a closed form. Together they show that the stored shares add up to the variance each node's predictors actually explain.

lmg_certificate() returns the larger of the two deviations: a value near zero confirms the decomposition, up to numerical precision.

certificate() reports the same value for a fitted network. The check does not verify the \(R^2\) of the individual subset regressions between the empty and the full model, and the sum identity alone would hold for any set of subset values; the closed form is what ties the full model to the data.

Usage

lmg_certificate(x)

Arguments

x

A relative-importance network from relimp_network() (psychnet).

Value

A single number, the larger of the two deviations; 0 for an exact decomposition.

Details

For outcome \(j\) with shares \(w_{kj}\) and full-model \(R^2_j\), the two deviations are \(\max_j |\sum_k w_{kj} - R^2_j|\) and \(\max_j |R^2_j - (1 - 1 / (S^{-1})_{jj})|\). When the correlation matrix \(S\) is singular (reciprocal condition number below 1e-12) the closed form does not exist and only the first deviation is returned. For a network with normalized = TRUE the unscaled shares are used.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when x is not a network from relimp_network().

See also

relimp_network(); certificate(); tmfg_certificate(), the other structural check.

Examples

S <- 0.4^abs(outer(1:5, 1:5, "-"))
lmg_certificate(relimp_network(cor_matrix = S))
#> [1] 5.551115e-17
